title: Model the cocoa purchasing process in BPMN
instructions:
## Tokens through gateways

At a cocoa buying station: a **farmer delivers beans**. The clerk **weighs the beans** and **grades the beans** at the same time (two people, in parallel). Then the station **checks the grade**: if the beans are accepted, the station **issues a receipt** and **pays the farmer**; otherwise it **returns the beans**. Either way the process ends.

## Do this

Write the BPMN process: a start event, tasks, a **parallel** gateway split (`{+}`) with a matching parallel join, an **exclusive** gateway (`{X Accepted?}`) with labelled flows and a matching exclusive join, and an end event. Put the clerk's and cashier's tasks in lanes if you like (`lane Clerk: A, B`).

hints: P1{+} is a parallel split; A --> P1, P1 --> W[Weigh beans], P1 --> G[Grade beans]; then W --> P2{+} and G --> P2 join them.
X1{X Accepted?} splits: X1 -->|yes| R[Issue receipt] and X1 -->|no| B[Return beans].
Both branches must reach the same exclusive join X2{X} before the end event: R --> Y[Pay farmer], Y --> X2, B --> X2, X2 --> E((End)).

checks.label: Weigh, grade, receipt, pay and return tasks
The accepted path issues a receipt
The rejected path returns the beans
BPMN rules: start and end events, gateways paired, nothing unreachable

realityNote: Mismatched gateways are the classic BPMN error: a parallel split closed by an exclusive join lets the process end twice; an exclusive split closed by a parallel join deadlocks, waiting for a token that never comes. Process engines like Camunda refuse such models.
